tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent with explicit example trigger phrases ('why is my CloudTrail bill so high', etc.), covers scope broadly including non-obvious phrasings, and remains a concise paragraph despite listing multiple triggers.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user asks to reduce, review, audit, or optimize CloudTrail spend, or reports an unexpected CloudTrail cost or usage increase. Activate on requests like "why is my CloudTrail bill so high", "reduce CloudTrail costs"...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is focused on domain-specific procedures (billing model summary, workflow steps, severity definitions, safety boundaries, quirks) rather than explaining general concepts the agent already knows. It stays concise and defers deep detail to reference files.
tests.evidence: Management events: the first copy per Region is free; every additional copy is billed. Duplicate management-event trails are the most common overspend.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body gives only a short summary of the billing model and workflow, consistently deferring detailed tables, API call lists, and check definitions to references/ files rather than inlining them, including within the conditional workflow steps.
tests.evidence: For the full charge-by-charge table and the detailed billing consequences the checks rely on, load references/billing-model.md when you need to decide whether a specific trail copy is free or paid, or to explain a charge.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three references/ files (billing-model.md, api-inventory.md, opportunities.md) are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a clear condition specifying when to load it (e.g., when deciding free vs paid, when inventorying, when analyzing opportunities).
tests.evidence: load references/billing-model.md when you need to decide whether a specific trail copy is free or paid, or to explain a charge.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All references/ links use relative paths from the skill root with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/compliance-sensitive operations (safety boundaries, dedup-vs-filtering interaction rule) get explicit, prescriptive rules, while flexible steps like collecting usage signals give the agent latitude to choose among signals based on availability.
tests.evidence: Never recommend reducing the single authoritative security trail below the organization's logging requirements. When in doubt, recommend converting a duplicate to data-events-only rather than deleting it.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: When multiple signals/tools are available for Step 3, the skill designates a clear preferred default (Cost Explorer) while listing others as alternatives.
tests.evidence: This is the most direct dollar signal — prefer it when the role has Cost Explorer access.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (scope identification, inventory, usage collection, analysis, validation, reporting) applicable to any CloudTrail cost review, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Identify target scope. Ask the user which accounts and Regions to review...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated 'Known Quirks' section with concrete, non-obvious corrections (free vs paid copies, shadow trails, dedup/filtering interaction).
tests.evidence: Organizations trails appear as shadow trails in member accounts — set includeShadowTrails=true and do not double-count them as member-created duplicates.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a structured report and provides a dedicated template asset for it.
tests.evidence: Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure, section order, and table schemas in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md).

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large output template is embedded inline in the body; only a small severity table is present, and the full report template is stored in assets/.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file report-template.md is referenced in the Step 6 workflow entry.
tests.evidence: Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure, section order, and table schemas in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md).

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies exactly when to load it — during report generation in Step 6.
tests.evidence: Load that template when generating the report.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The workflow is presented as an ordered checklist using '- [ ] Step N:' format for all six steps, matching the required format.
tests.evidence: - [ ] **Step 1: Identify target scope.** ... - [ ] **Step 2: Inventory trails and event data stores.**

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 5 explicitly instructs the agent to self-check findings for errors (double-counting, misapplied filtering, unsupported dollar estimates) before producing the report.
tests.evidence: Step 5: Validate findings. Before writing the report, self-check the findings: confirm no finding double-counts savings already captured by a §4.1 dedup, verify each management-event filtering finding applies only to a paid copy that is being kept...
